Urviksten (Z15)

Scoring-table region: Wescann / Gerudia.

In one sentence: hold the last northern Ebonfrost domain, rebuild its Black Pine fleet and Ebonsteel, and pursue the dynastic war that can restore Black Castanor.

Story: high | Mission-tree length: medium-long (41 direct missions) | Mission-tree update: current local version v1.37.5.0; exact rework date unresolved | Uniqueness: high | Grind: medium-high | Early pressure: high | Expansion ability: high.

1444 starting position

This map is a static local-Mod history snapshot for 11 November 1444. It does not execute opening events; gold marks the displayed Tag’s actual non-water holdings.

Urviksten (Z15)

1444 starting territory. Displayed Tag: Z15.

Complete game region: Cannor; displayed Tag: Z15, panel 1/1, showing five provinces. The white capital dot marks the centre of the capital province only.

The northern remnant of an old dynasty

In 1444 Urviksten is an existing Gerudian domain, not a Tag waiting to be formed. It is ruled by Karl II Ebonfrost, whose history block gives him strong military ability and the Strict and Cruel traits; Gunnar is already in the succession line. The country uses Olavish culture, Skaldhyrric faith, and its dedicated Urvikstener Despotism reform. These are direct facts from the current history files. [Local history script]

The offline English Wiki places this small country within the longer history of the Ebonfrost dynasty. Its ancestors relied on Black Frost and Ebonsteel, building a northern kingship connected to old Castanor before a long decline. In 1417 Lord Johan died during the attack on Naugsvol, and Karl II began the Black Frost War, taking the shipbuilding timber of the Black Pines. During the 1420s the Greytide moved south; Castan closed the passes against the Frozenmaw Orcs and temporarily made peace with an old enemy. Small raids still troubled the frontier in 1444. These setting events do not prove that a player has already achieved the future restoration goal. [Wiki material]

The opening contradiction is clear: Urviksten has the political memory of an old dynasty but not the power to match it. Northern naval power, inland border defence, and southern Orcish pressure all fall on one remote domain. Karl’s hard personality begins the restoration story and can also make that restoration dangerous. War, monarchy, and restoration claims are not automatically evil; treatment of residents, enemies, and subjects depends on the actual policy. [Local history script] [Wiki material]

Restoration route and formation boundary

The 41 direct missions centre on Urviksten and cover Black Pine trade and fleets, northern settlement, Ebonsteel craft, Ebonfrost authority, and the advance toward the old Castanorian core. The opening task is to survive northern neighbours and Frozenmaw pressure while accumulating ports, an army, and money. Later goals look less like ordinary border expansion and more like a political and geographic foundation for Black Castanorian succession. [Local script]

Black Castanor (Z34) is not Urviksten’s 1444 name and is not an automatic alias granted by one mission. The formation decision requires specific territory, trials, and other qualifications before the Tag changes. Current mission potential allows the original Z15 to keep using the Urviksten missions after forming Z34; this does not establish a separate verified Z34-exclusive tree. Dynastic restoration is a campaign future, not an outcome that occurs in every run. [Local script]

Why the campaign feels different

The first distinction is multi-front northern pressure. On land you must hold passes and answer Orcs and neighbours; at sea you must develop the Black Pines and a fleet. Focusing on one side exposes the other. Two player posts identify Frozenmaw, Bjarnrik, and Gawed as common pressure sources, but their war order is version-bound personal experience rather than a scripted opening rule. [Local script] [Community view]

The second is the Ebonsteel legacy. With the required Lions of the North DLC, the history gives an Ebonsteel stockpile; decisions also cover rediscovery, improved craft, and major financial investment. Restoration is therefore not only a claim map but an armaments project that needs resources, technology, and industry. Without the DLC, money, or the relevant stage, the complete craft cannot be treated as a free opening advantage. [Local script]

The third is the combination of dynasty and formation. Many formables are generic buttons available to any qualifying predecessor; Urviksten’s missions instead build a more specific identity around the Ebonfrost family, the old empire, and frontier war. The player must choose between northern expansion and a turn toward the old capital while balancing money, army, and port development. It suits a difficult restoration campaign, not relaxed development that avoids strong neighbours. [Local script]

Personality and evidence boundary

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 88/100 | Authoritarianism 82/100 | Magic–Artifice 35/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 32/100) | Pluralism 42/100.

The v2.1 value assessment is neutral (51/100) with a mixed trajectory. Resistance to raids and protection of the country are concrete public aims, while Karl’s cruel personality, hard monarchy, and revenge setting limit a high score. War and monarchy are not deductions by themselves; later occupation policy was not fully checked. The detailed provenance and unresolved boundaries are recorded on the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces native English national-idea names and descriptions alongside the inherited source displays. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Successor ideas do not stack automatically with the predecessor set. Descriptions may recount history or depict a future ideal, not events already completed in 1444. Native English prose is used rather than back-translating the Chinese localisation; any inherited display/unit uncertainty remains unresolved.

Urviksten (Z15) — Urvikstener Ideas

Applicable condition (alternative, not a stacked set):

    trigger = {
        tag = Z15
    }

Traditions: Urvikstener Traditions

Effects: Coastal raiding: allowed; Leader land shock: +1.

Idea 1: The Giants Tears

Past the mountains and vales of Urviksten lies an expansive, forbidding mireland known as the Giants Tears. These lands are harsh and unforgiving, long being a land unpopulated except for the hardiest of individuals. But now the Giant's Tears are inhabited by orcs, vile creatures. Urviksten must secure this frontier against them.

Effects: Colonists: +1; On idea completion: remove the temporary colonist.

        effect = { remove_temporary_colonist = yes }

Idea 2: Legacy of Castan Ebonfrost

Castan Ebonfrost, legendary conqueror of Escann, conquerer of Castanor, was born and raised in Urviksten. While he left this land with his followers and the famous black dragon, his dynasty lives on in Urviksten. After his demise, one of Castanor's sons, Urvik, returned to Urviksten with an army of his own to retake the homeland. Since then Urviksten has retained the strict and disciplined army tactics of Castan Ebonfrost's army.

Effects: Army drill gain modifier: +5%.

Idea 3: Black Pines, Black Frost

While the fjords of Urviksten are cold, unforgiving and bleak, they are full of natural resources, especially prime timber. Unique with their black trunks, the Black Pines of the Black Frost Mountains are hard as iron, although with the right technique can easily be felled. Not only useful for ships, they are also excellent for improving production due to their increased toughness.

Effects: Production efficiency: +5%; Ship durability: +2.5%.

Idea 4: Orcish Scum

To the south, in the Giants Tears and in Castanor, vast hordes of orcish scum rampage across the lands. While they may have destroyed the ancient and powerful lands to the south, the descendants of Castan Ebonfrost are more than powerful enough to remove these filth. You need only apply force where needed, and shove elsewhere.

Effects: Culture conversion cost: -20%.

Idea 5: Pale Banners

Banners waving in the wind, as pale as fresh snow, emblazoned with the black dragon of Castan Ebonfrost, wave above the armies of Urviksten. Possessing a vast military, Urviksten is more of a military with a state attached than a state with an army. The economy and politics of Urviksten are all focused to make the army as efficient, and numerous, as possible.

Effects: Land force limit modifier: +10%; Land maintenance modifier: -10%.

Idea 6: Ebonsteel Armory

The prize of Urviksten, and of Castanor in the past, the Ebonsteel Armory is a vast foundry, blacksmith and armory supplying high quality weapons and armor made of Ebonsteel, a dark naturally alloyed metal found throughout Urviksten.

Effects: shock_damage_received：-5%; Shock damage: +10%.

Idea 7: Claims of Castanor

Castan Ebonfrost conquered Escann, Castanor and even Vertesk. All these lands rightfully belong to Urviksten, heirs to Castanor. The Black Dragon Banner will wave from the Silvermere to the Dameshead Sea once more!

Effects: Core-creation cost: -15%.

Ambition: Urvikstener Ambition

Effects: Administrative efficiency: +5%.

Black Castanor (Z34) — Black Castanorian Ideas

Applicable condition (alternative, not a stacked set):

    trigger = {
        tag = Z34
    }

Traditions: Black Castanorian Traditions

Effects: Army drill gain modifier: +5%; Administrative efficiency: +5%.

Idea 1: Conqueror of Escann

Castan Ebonfrost was the legendary conqueror of Castanor, hailing from the cold lands of Urviksten. In his youth he was a lowborn Reaver who rose the ranks after many years of raiding. Word of his exploits spread across the lands, and in 865 he was awarded the dominion of Vrorenmarch as a ploy by Castanor.

A year later he smashed through Castanor with his armies and killed Castan XLVIII, and crowned himself as the new Castan of Castanor. He did so by sacking the temple of Castellos on the Trialmount, which guards and administers the trials which decide the leader of Castanor, known as Castan. Afterwards, the only individuals allowed to take the trials were descendents of the Ebonfrost dynasty, maintained by the Ebon Guard.

Effects: Years of separatism: -5.

Idea 2: Ebon Guard

The Ebon Guard were the elite military force of Black Castanor, answering only to Castan Ebonfrost and his successors. Outfitted with Ebonsteel armor and weaponry, they were feared throughout the world. The Ebon Guard was primarily made up of strong Gerudians of Ebonmarck, although some of the native Escanni that proved worthy were given the privilege of joining the Guard. Most famous for guarding the Trialmount, the Ebon Guard also served in military maneuvers that required only the best of the best.

Effects: Army morale: +10%; Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Idea 3: Ebonfrost's Fist

A legendary artifact, Ebonfrost's Fist was a magical gauntlet infused with the strength of golems. Famous for his explosive anger, Castan Ebonfrost wore this gauntlet to smash tables to make his point clear, or to make his point even more clear by beating his opposition into submission.

Effects: Yearly absolutism: +1.

Idea 4: Successor of Castanor

Black Castanor conquered far and wide, from the Serpentspine Mountains to Vertesk on the Dameshead Sea. No empire had boasted such a claim since the glory days of old Castanor. Although these lands have gone astray after the disintegration of Black Castanor following the War of the Sorcerer-King, none can deny the ancient bounds of our empire. With Black Castanor restored, we should utilize these extensive claims to restore our realm beyond Escann!

Effects: Core-creation cost: -20%.

Idea 5: Ebonsteel Foundries

One of the most important innovations of Black Castanor, Ebonsteel paved the way for the extensive conquest and pacification of lands by Black Castanor. A special steel-like black alloy, lighter and stronger than already-rare steel, can be found in the Black Frost mountains of Urviksten, but can also be created with a special combination of metals and minerals. With this art reborn, the armies of Black Castanor will once more conquer the lands bearing this superior steel.

Effects: Production efficiency: +10%; shock_damage_received：-10%.

Idea 6: Black Reaver Academy

Black Castanor was founded by Reavers, both in the past and in the new restoration of the realm. These legendary warriors formed the first generation of soldiers that conquered the land, and in order to preserve this advantage Castan Ebonfrost established the Black Reaver Academy. This Academy trained the officers of the realm in the art of war, in the Gerudian way that is unique and strange to the Escanni. Although it was ransacked and razed by the League of so-called Free Realms at the end of the War of the Sorcerer-King, we have rebuilt this magnificent institution to ensure that our martial heritage may never be lost!

Effects: Army tradition: +1.

Idea 7: Military Renewal Act

One of the staples of warfare is a constant supply of manpower. Castanor in the days of the Ebonfrost were plagued by treasonous lords who thwarted our rightful rule both openly and behind closed doors. Even centuries later, even after the destruction of the Escanni by the Greentide, the land still harbors traitors. In order to subdue the pretenders and retake our rightful lands, an act must be passed to make sure that our reserves are always full by enforcing conscription. The lords and nobility will no longer be able to hamper our efforts any more.

Effects: Manpower recovery speed: +20%.

Ambition: Black Castanorian Ambition

Effects: Global trade power: +15%.
